limitations: Seven PR admission lanes, four mandatory Quint partitions on main PR/merge-queue contexts, and one production main Full admission with two attempts and three independent predicates (exact GitHub identity, complete current-source rows, staging certification). Other PR branches require Quint skipped. Actual canonical CI also requires the four-shard aggregate on main push/manual/reusable contexts regardless of changed paths.

GitHub supplies trustworthy run/artifact metadata for the requested repository and protects workflow source at its exact SHA. The hook executes real YAML result shell gates, all event/branch classifiers, source-bound shard validation, actual Git manifest/ZIP consumers and existing ledger/staging tests with controlled API fixtures. Production gates run at migration/image/Worker/Pages mutation boundaries. Admission linearizes at final metadata recheck; a future rerun after admission does not retroactively revoke an already-started effect.

Finite boolean identity/row/staging projection and at most one concurrent rerun; file bytes/hashes, arbitrary API histories, network failure timing and provider effects are outside the model. Tests exercise real Git/ZIP/current manifest code with synthetic GitHub responses; no actual GitHub dispatch/deployment, branch protection deployment, physical device or service availability claim. Current expected manifest is recomputed from the trusted exact-source checkout. Fair completion assumes reads/decisions return; unavailable GitHub remains fail closed.
